method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the 'Q fever' chapter of the Australian Immunisation Handbook, retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- health.gov.au states 'all other rights are reserved'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the Stroke Foundation, Kidney Health Australia and NHFA/CSANZ sources already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Q fever vaccine is recommended from age 15 for people at risk of *Coxiella burnetii* infection who have not had previous Q fever infection or vaccination.**
claims.source_text: Q fever vaccine is recommended for people aged ≥15 years who are at risk of infection with C. burnetii and have not had previous Q fever infection or vaccination.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Q fever', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/q-fever, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **At-risk occupations:** abattoir workers · farmers · stockyard workers · shearers · transporters of cattle, camels, sheep, goats and kangaroos · vets, vet nurses and students · professional dog and cat breeders · pet food workers · agricultural college staff and students · wildlife and zoo workers with kangaroos and bandicoots · animal refuge and shelter workers · people who cull or process kangaroos or camels · laboratory workers with veterinary specimens.
claims.source_text: abattoir workers farmers stockyard workers shearers animal transporters (of high-risk animals such as cattle, camels, sheep, goats and kangaroos) veterinarians, veterinary nurses and veterinary students professional dog and cat breeders pet food manufacturing workers agricultural college staff and students wildlife and zoo workers who work with high-risk animals, including kangaroos and bandicoots animal refuge workers (including those working in animal shelters and boarding facilities) people who cull or process kangaroos or camels laboratory workers who handle veterinary specimens
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Q fever', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/q-fever, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pre-vaccination screening is required.** The Q-Vax product information says it is for **adults**; **ATAGI says it can be used from age 15**.
claims.source_text: pre-vaccination screening. The product information for Q-Vax states that this vaccine is for vaccination of adults. ATAGI recommends that Q-Vax can be used in people aged ≥15 years.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Q fever', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/q-fever, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Q fever is notifiable in every state and territory.**
claims.source_text: notifiable disease in all states and territories in Australia.
claims.locator: Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 'Q fever', The Australian Immunisation Handbook, at https://immunisationhandbook.health.gov.au/contents/vaccine-preventable-diseases/q-fever, retrieved 2026-09-23
